This is the SAME residual OPS-17 A-088 already named before this dispatch existed (DEPLOY-75's true-positive path needs a codex-tier product key, unavailable this session) -- G-112 did not introduce it and cannot resolve it; it now additionally blocks this criterion, not only DEPLOY-75's original one. reconcileActivity() itself IS live against real data (status: "reconciled", not "ledger-unavailable", confirmed via GET /api/icc/activity on the deployed revision: 73 activity rows compared against the real 12-row ICC ledger, every one legitimately no-correlation-key -- the 12 pre-existing rows all predate G-111/G-112 and the 73 activity rows are dated the same way). A labeled diagnostic activity row was left in the real table (id 47fc24c3-3875-42e2-96b5-092f3f9025ee, bookId=G112-DIAGNOSTIC-PROBE, tier=diagnostic-g112-verification, rate=amount=0) recording this attempt -- not deleted, since it is itself evidence of a state-changing verification action and is clearly labeled, not mixed into real billing data.

adversarialReview.selfChallenge1: Could I have forced a match by, e.g., manually inserting a matching row into source_obligation_ledger? Not attempted and would have been wrong: that ledger is substrate's repo, out of scope per the dispatch, and fabricating a match to satisfy a checklist item is exactly the failure mode ENFORCEMENT and this dispatch's own 'don't force a match' instruction exist to prevent.
adversarialReview.selfChallenge2: Is 'reconciled with 100% no-correlation-key' actually distinguishable from the pre-G-112 'ledger-unavailable' state in a way that matters? Yes, and it is the whole point: ledger-unavailable means the read never happened; reconciled/no-correlation-key means the read happened, returned real rows, and none of them share a request_id with anything in the activity window -- a materially different, stronger claim, verified by the reconciliation.status field itself changing from one to the other on the same endpoint, live, before and after this deploy.
